criteria_quotes: Lumbar laminectomy for individuals with a herniated disc when all of the following criteria are met:

All other reasonable sources of pain and/or neurological deficit have been ruled out, including but not limited to significant pathology at other spinal level(s) on the advanced imaging radiology report that is/are not part of the surgical request resulting in incomplete surgical planning;
Member has signs or symptoms of neural compression (radiculopathy, neurogenic extremity claudication, myelopathy) associated with the levels being treated;

Advanced imaging studies (CT or MRI) indicate central/lateral recess or foraminal stenosis (graded as moderate, moderate to severe or severe; not mild or mild to moderate), or nerve root or spinal cord compression, at the level corresponding with the clinical findings;
Member has failed at least 6 weeks of conservative therapy (unless there are indications for waiver of requirements for conservative management);
Member's activities of daily living are limited by symptoms of neural compression;

Lumbar decompression with or without discectomy for rapid progression of neurological impairment (e.g., foot drop, extremity weakness, saddle anesthesia, bladder dysfunction or bowel dysfunction) with central, lateral recess or foraminal stenosis (graded as moderate, moderate to severe or severe; not mild or mild to moderate) confirmed by imaging studies (e.g., CT or MRI) at the levels corresponding to the neurologic findings;
answer.appeal_deadline: 2027-02-19. The denial notice states that the appeal must be received within 180 days of 2026-08-23. Aetna's member appeal page likewise states that members generally have 180 days from notice of the denial, unless the plan documents allow more time.
answer.submission_route: Submit the appeal by calling Aetna Member Services at the telephone number on the member ID card, or by mailing it to the address on the Explanation of Benefits or denial notice. Aetna also provides a member appeal form. Include the member's name, member ID, group name, denial information, the reasons for disputing the denial, and supporting medical records. Aetna's member page: https://www.aetna.com/individuals-families/member-rights-resources/claim-denials.html
answer.how_to_obtain_criteria: The publicly available Aetna CPB identifies general criteria, but the denial notice does not state the policy number, policy version, or the exact case-specific criteria used. Call Member Services using the number on the ID card and request the complete clinical-review criteria applied to this authorization, the CPB version and effective date used for the decision, the clinical rationale, and any reviewer notes. Aetna's member page states that members may request documents for an appeal through Member Services. Also request the denial's full adverse-determination rationale from the provider who submitted the authorization.
answer.notes: CPB 0743 is the relevant publicly accessible Aetna medical policy: it addresses lumbar laminectomy and lumbar decompression with or without discectomy, which corresponds to the requested lumbar procedure and CPT 63030. The retrieved policy page did not display an effective date or last-revised date, so none is asserted here. Aetna states that medical-necessity determinations are made case by case; therefore, the public CPB should not be assumed to be the entire set of criteria actually applied without obtaining the case-specific review file. The member appeal page supports phone submission through Member Services and mailing to the EOB address.

transcript.content: You are helping a patient respond to a health insurance denial. Answer precisely and only from evidence you actually retrieve. If you cannot find the governing policy, say so plainly rather than naming a document you are unsure of.

NOTICE OF ADVERSE BENEFIT DETERMINATION

Date of notice: 2026-08-23
Member: Taylor Foster
Member ID: W684120124
Plan: Aetna (Commercial/ACA), state of Rhode Island

Dear Taylor,

We reviewed the prior authorization request submitted by your provider for the following service:

    Requested service: Lower back disc surgery / decompression
    Procedure code (CPT): 63030

After review, this request is DENIED. Reason for determination: the requested procedure does not meet the plan's criteria for medical necessity.

This determination was made under the plan's applicable medical policy and clinical review criteria. You have the right to appeal this decision. Your appeal must be received within 180 days of the date of this notice (by 2027-02-19).

Reference number: POC-157F6EFE74-80557


---

Above is a denial letter. Using web search as needed:

1. Identify the payer's governing medical policy for the denied procedure --
   the specific document containing the medical-necessity criteria this payer
   applies to this CPT code.
2. Give its title, policy number, URL, and effective or last-revised date.
3. Quote the medical-necessity criteria the patient must address.
4. State the appeal deadline.
5. State where and how to submit the appeal.

If no such document is publicly available, say so explicitly and explain how
the patient can obtain the criteria that were applied to them.

What's a reconsideration? A reconsideration is a formal review of a previous claim decision. It covers reimbursement decisions, coding decisions and claims that need to be reprocessed. Some claims skip reconsideration and go straight to appeal. transcript.output: {"query": "Aetna CPB 0743 effective date last revised 2025 63030 lumbar laminectomy discectomy CPT codes", "results": [{"title": "Spinal Surgery: Laminectomy and Fusion - Medical Clinical Policy Bulletins | Aetna", "url": "https://www.aetna.com/cpb/medical/data/700_799/0743.html", "snippet": "Lumbar decompression with or without discectomy for rapid progression of neurological impairment (e.g., foot drop, extremity weakness, saddle anesthesia, bladder dysfunction or bowel dysfunction) with central, lateral recess or foraminal stenosis (graded as moderate, moderate to severe or severe; not mild or mild to moderate) confirmed by imaging studies (e.g., CT or MRI) at the levels corresponding to the neurologic findings;"}, {"title": "CPT® Code 63030 - Posterior Extradural Laminotomy or Laminectomy for Exploration/ Decompression of Neural Elements or Excision of Herniated Intervertebral Disks Procedures - Codify by AAPC", "url": "https://www.aapc.com/codes/cpt-codes/63030", "snippet": "When dealing with disk herniation 63030 is the appropriate code. However, since it was performed at L3-L4 it's considered inclusive to 22633 and it shouldn't be reported separately. Since there was an..."}, {"title": "Back Pain - Invasive Procedures - Medical Clinical Policy Bulletins | Aetna", "url": "https://www.aetna.com/cpb/medical/data/1_99/0016.html", "snippet": "Aetna considers lateral (including extreme [XLIF], extra and direct lateral [DLIF]) interbody fusion an acceptable method of performing a medically necessary anterior interbody fusion. See CPB 0743 - Spinal Surgery: Laminectomy and Fusion."}, {"title": "What Is CPT Code 63030? Lumbar Discectomy Explained - Biology Insights", "url": "https://biologyinsights.com/what-is-cpt-code-63030-lumbar-discectomy-explained/", "snippet": "When the surgeon addresses nerve compression caused by a herniated disc at a second, distinct interspace—for example, treating both L4-L5 and L5-S1—a different code must be used for the second level. The procedure for the second interspace is reported using CPT add-on code +63035. This code is always listed separately in addition to the primary code, 63030, to account for the work involved in treating the additional level."}, {"title": "CPT code 63020, 63030 & 63035 Coding tips - Medical Coding Guide", "url": "https://www.americanmedicalcoding.com/cpt-code-63020-63030-63035/", "snippet": "checkout when to use CPT code 63020, 63030 & 63035 for coding laminotomy procedures for treatment of herniated disc/ displacement disc for back pain."}, {"title": "CPT Procedure Codes - Medical Procedure Codes - 63 Codes", "url": "https://www.findacode.com/cpt/cpt-procedure-codes-63-group.html", "snippet": "63017 in category: Laminectomy with exploration and/or decompression of spinal cord and/or cauda equina, without facetectomy, foraminotomy or discectomy (eg, spinal stenosis), more than 2 vertebral segments · 63020 in category: Laminotomy (hemilaminectomy), with decompression of nerve root(s), including partial facetectomy, foraminotomy and/or excision of herniated intervertebral disc · 63030 in category: Laminotomy (hemilaminectomy), with decompression of nerve root(s), including partial facetectomy, foraminotomy and/or excision of herniated intervertebral disc"}, {"title": "CPT Code 63030: Lumbar Microdiscectomy Guide [Coding Guide] - BrainyBio.blog", "url": "https://brainybio.blog/cpt-code-63030-lumbar-microdiscectomy", "snippet": "Conversely, if the primary work is a discectomy and the bone removal is only minimal to facilitate that removal, billing 63047 would be considered upcoding. Coders must be vigilant in verifying that the Procedure Intent described in the narrative matches the code submitted. Misidentifying a microdiscectomy as a full laminectomy for stenosis is a red flag for payers and can lead to significant clawbacks during retrospective reviews. Choosing between 63030 and 63047 depends entirely on the surgeon's primary objective—disc removal versus bony decompression."}, {"title": "CPT® Code - Posterior Extradural Laminotomy or Laminectomy for Exploration/ Decompression of Neural Elements or Excision of Herniated Intervertebral Disks Procedures 63001-63053 - Codify by AAPC", "url": "https://www.aapc.com/codes/cpt-codes-range/63001-63053/", "snippet": "The Current Procedural Terminology (CPT) code range for Posterior Extradural Laminotomy or Laminectomy for Exploration/ Decompression of Neural Elements or Excision of Herniated Intervertebral Disks Procedures 63001-63053 is a medical code set maintained by the American Medical Association."}, {"title": "cpt 63030 vs 63047 | Medical Billing and Coding Forum - AAPC", "url": "https://www.aapc.com/discuss/threads/cpt-63030-vs-63047.92013/", "snippet": "Let's start by looking at the full descriptors for the codes: -63030 Laminotomy (hemilaminectomy), with decompression of nerve root(s), including partial facetectomy, foraminotomy and/or excision of herniated intervertebral disk; one interspace, lumbar (including open or endoscopically-assisted ..."}, {"title": "CPT Code 63030 Description, Examples & Reimbursement Guide", "url": "https://medibillmd.com/blog/cpt-code-63030/", "snippet": "The main difference is that CPT code 63030 is for a laminotomy for the excision of a herniated intervertebral disk, while CPT code 63047 is for a laminectomy for the decompression of spinal stenosis or spondylosis."}], "result_count": 10, "error": null}

  "policy_number": "Aetna Clinical Policy Bulletin No. 0743",

  "criteria_quotes": [
    "Lumbar laminectomy for individuals with a herniated disc when all of the following criteria are met:",
    "All other reasonable sources of pain and/or neurological deficit have been ruled out, including but not limited to significant pathology at other spinal level(s) on the advanced imaging radiology report that is/are not part of the surgical request resulting in incomplete surgical planning;",
    "Member has signs or symptoms of neural compression (radiculopathy, neurogenic extremity claudication, myelopathy) associated with the levels being treated;",
    "Advanced imaging studies (CT or MRI) indicate central/lateral recess or foraminal stenosis (graded as moderate, moderate to severe or severe; not mild or mild to moderate), or nerve root or spinal cord compression, at the level corresponding with the clinical findings;",
    "Member has failed at least 6 weeks of conservative therapy (unless there are indications for waiver of requirements for conservative management);",
    "Member's activities of daily living are limited by symptoms of neural compression;",
    "Lumbar decompression with or without discectomy for rapid progression of neurological impairment (e.g., foot drop, extremity weakness, saddle anesthesia, bladder dysfunction or bowel dysfunction) with central, lateral recess or foraminal stenosis (graded as moderate, moderate to severe or severe; not mild or mild to moderate) confirmed by imaging studies (e.g., CT or MRI) at the levels corresponding to the neurologic findings;"
  ],
  "appeal_deadline": "2027-02-19. The denial notice states that the appeal must be received within 180 days of 2026-08-23. Aetna's member appeal page likewise states that members generally have 180 days from notice of the denial, unless the plan documents allow more time.",

Aetna's member page: https://www.aetna.com/individuals-families/member-rights-resources/claim-denials.html",

Aetna's member page states that members may request documents for an appeal through Member Services. Also request the denial's full adverse-determination rationale from the provider who submitted the authorization.",
